entities.name: Actinic keratosis
observations: Actinic keratosis is the most commonly recognized precursor or associated premalignant lesion for conventional invasive cutaneous SCC in chronically sun-damaged skin.
Individual AK lesions usually do not progress; reported progression estimates vary widely, approximately 0.025%–16% per lesion-year across older studies.
AK is a visible marker of a carcinogenic sun-damaged field, but invasive cutaneous SCC can arise without a clinically recognized preceding AK.

entities.name: Actinic keratosis grade I
observations: AK I is a histopathologic severity grade rather than a separate lesion.
AK I denotes mild atypia mainly in basal and immediate suprabasal layers, approximately the lower third of the epidermis.

entities.name: Cutaneous SCC in situ
observations: SCC in situ, also called Bowen disease, is another major precursor lesion for invasive cutaneous SCC and represents a more advanced intraepidermal neoplastic process than ordinary AK.
